label: Sparrow (small hobby, B6-6)
description: Generic small 18 mm-motor sport rocket on an Estes B6-6: BT-20-size body tube (18.7 mm), light balsa fins, 10 in plastic chute deployed by the motor's 6 s ejection charge.

notes.mass: 22 g airframe + chute + wadding, typical for a ~30 cm BT-20 kit
notes.cd: 0.70: small rockets run at low Reynolds number with proportionally large fins and launch lugs, so their total Cd is higher than the 0.5-0.6 of larger rockets
notes.recovery: single 10 in chute; a ~40 g rocket descends at ~4 m/s, fine for grass
notes.delay: 6 s: true (chute-free) apogee comes 5.8 s after burnout; the common B6-4 would open the chute ~1.8 s early

notes.backup_timer_s: nominal true apogee + max(1.0 s, 4 sigma of the apogee time under the standard dispersions), from lift-off; the C6 value 8.5 s follows the same rule (7.42 + 1.08)
notes.max_boost_s: longest burn x 1.6 (C6: 1.86 s -> 3.0 s): burnout fallback for a stuck accelerometer
notes.min_deploy_after_launch_s: final burnout x 1.35 (C6: 1.86 s -> 2.5 s): deploy inhibit
notes.basis: B6 burn 0.86 s; true apogee 6.69 s (sigma 0.12 s under dispersions); peak specific force ~34 g briefly saturates the +-24 g sensor (harmless, exempt from the stuck-sensor test)
notes.motor: B6-6 is the longest B6 delay: its charge fires ~0.17 s after true apogee, nearly together with the FC, so on this rocket the backup is almost simultaneous
notes.powered_jerk_psd: 1e4 m^2/s^5 under thrust and for 0.5 s after each detected burnout (tail-off): the coast q (10) cannot follow thrust-curve and tail-off jerk on this rocket, the gate then rejected genuine samples and nominal flights went 'inconsistent' (found by the fleet SIL runs; see fc/include/fc/config.hpp). 1e4 sits in the measured plateau: apogee detection +0.04-0.05 s on every preset
